brief: Answers questions about a text as prose: its words, sentences, paragraphs and lines, its writing systems, and common clean-ups.
detail: stzString builds one of these to answer Script, Words and the other text-level questions; build one directly with a text, or use stzText, which inherits from it and adds meaning-level methods. Words, sentences and lines follow the Unicode rules, so Hebrew, Arabic, Chinese and emoji text is segmented where a reader would expect. Verbs such as ReverseWords and Simplify change the held text in place and return nothing (the Q form returns the object so calls chain), and the past-tense form (WordsReversed, Simplified) returns the new text and leaves the object alone. Pass a plain text, not a stzString: the first edit made through the object empties the stzString that was passed in. Known defects today: UniqueWords keeps the punctuation stuck to a word, so ContainsWord misses it; ReverseEachWord and EachWordReversed break any non-ASCII word; OnlyScript, OnlyArabic and OnlyLatin raise errors; ToSentenceCase capitalizes only the first letter.
receiver: o1 = new stzStringText("the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog")
example: #--> dog lazy the over jumps fox brown quick the
